title: Kernel fingerprint routing for heterogeneous MIG topologies and clock states
creator: Jonah Kim
description:
Background:
Our serving runtime currently picks kernel variants using a static heuristic primarily based on model size and batch. As we support more heterogeneous GPU shapes (H100/L40S/A10) and increasingly fragmented MIG partitions, we've observed wide variance in per-kernel latency depending on (a) MIG slice shape, (b) active GPU clock/power state, and (c) sequence-length distribution for prefill vs decode. This results in suboptimal kernel choices for a significant fraction of live requests and prevents us from achieving consistent latency SLOs across deployments.

Goal:
Create an automated fingerprinting and routing system that: (1) builds a compact performance fingerprint for kernel variants across MIG topologies and clock states, (2) surfaces a runtime routing table that maps request characteristics (MIG shape, sequence-length distribution, batch size) to preferred kernel+packing strategy, and (3) integrates with the prefill/decode scheduler to prefer low-latency kernels for initial token generation while preserving throughput for long-form decoding.

Success metrics (service-level):
- Reduce median token latency for small-batch prefill on H100 MIG slices by >=20% compared to baseline.
- Reduce 99th percentile latency regressions caused by suboptimal kernel choices on L40S by >=30%.
- No customer-visible correctness regressions (KV cache and attention semantics intact).

Approach:
1) Offline microbench profiler: run sweeps across target hardware (H100 80GB full, H100 MIG shapes, L40S, A10) measuring kernel variants across sequence lengths [8, 32, 128, 512], batch sizes [1,2,4,8], and clock governors (stock, sustained-power, perf). Generate a fingerprint record keyed by (gpu_family, mig_shape, clock_state, seq_len_bucket, batch_bucket) -> best kernel id + perf metrics.
2) Fingerprint compression: reduce records to compact routing rules by clustering adjacent seq_len/batch buckets where the same kernel wins.
3) Runtime routing: implement a lightweight matcher that selects the kernel variant at request dispatch time using the fingerprint table. The matcher falls back to the current heuristic if no fingerprint exists.
4) Prefill/decode integration: extend the scheduler to consult the matcher during prefill phase and optionally pin a kernel-id for the subsequent decode to avoid expensive kernel-switch handshakes.
5) Safety and rollback: preserve a configurable confidence threshold and runtime telemetry to revert to baseline heuristic for specific models/customers.

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In-scope: H100 (full + MIG shapes), L40S, A10; kernel variants we ship today; scheduler changes for prefill/decode handshake; offline profiler and routing table upload flow.
- Out-of-scope: automatic GPU clock changes (we will emit hints for the ops team but not change clocks from the control plane in this ticket), model-rewrite or quantization changes.

Deliverables:
- Microbench profiler job and dataset for H100/L40S/A10 (artifact uploaded to perf-bucket).
- Fingerprint compression library and format (RFC in docs).
- Runtime matcher + integration tests.
- Canary + rollout plan with dashboards and telemetry.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end flow from profiler to routing table to runtime selection works in dev cluster.
- Canary on dedicated pool shows targeted latency improvements and no correctness issues for 48h.
- PRs merged for profiler, matcher, scheduler and integration tests.

Risks and mitigations:
- Kernel handshake cost may negate gains for high-frequency decode transitions: mitigation is to pin kernel for the full request and only enable kernel-switching when predicted benefit > handshake cost.
- Fingerprints may become stale with new drivers/firmware: include fingerprint versioning and automated re-profiling triggers (post-driver updates).
comments: 2025-11-01 Jonah Kim: Triage done. Initial spike shows H100 1g.5p MIG shape prefers kernel-v17 for seq<=32 while full 80GB prefers kernel-v12. Need systematic sweep to verify.

2025-11-04 Maya Patel: Ran profiler jobs on H100 and L40S nodes (jobs/perf/ENG-67920). Preliminary numbers: H100 MIG 2g p50 per-token prefill reduced from 14.2ms -> 10.8ms (kernel-v17). L40S long decode unchanged but p99 reduced by 18% with packing changes.

2025-11-06 Maya Patel: Design RFC posted: internal docs/runtime/kernel-fingerprint-rfc.md (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Fingerprint+RFC). Seeking review from infra and runtime teams.

2025-11-08 Infra review (Danielle Ortiz): Raised concern about fingerprint size for fleets. Action: add compression step and TTL for routing entries. Also requested a safety flag to disable routing per-customer.
2025-11-10 Maya Patel: Implementation PR for matcher and routing table format opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567. Unit tests added for fallback behavior.

2025-11-12 Jonah Kim: Canary configuration created for dedicated-mig-small-pool. Observability dashboard (link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ENG-67920) includes kernel selection counts, p50/p99 token latency, and kernel-switch overhead. Plan canary run for 72h starting 2025-11-13.
2025-11-12 Maya Patel: Noted dependency on prefetch KV cache handshake changes from ENG-34210 to ensure pinned kernel doesn't conflict with cache layout; added dependency list.
(To do) Post-canary: capture live regressions by model and add auto-rollout thresholds in console rollout policies.
notes: Profiler artifacts uploaded to gs://perf-bucket/ENG-67920/ and a small dashboard created for quick iteration.
qa_steps: 1) Run profiler job in staging for target shapes. 2) Upload routing table to staging runtime. 3) Run canary traffic for 48-72h and monitor kernel-switch rate + latency. 4) Run model correctness suite to verify KV cache and attention outputs.
observability_plan: Add kernel_id tag to per-request traces, emit kernel_latency histogram and kernel_switch_duration. Create alert if kernel_switch_duration > 5ms or if p95 increases >10% during canary.
rollback_plan: 1) Disable routing via runtime feature flag. 2) Revert canary pool to baseline kernel heuristic. 3) If widespread, revert routing table upload and open incident for investigation.
